title: A bigger Solaris Client, better Discord, hosting and skin fixes

entries.text: 8 new HUD pieces: armor with durability, potion effects with time left, speed, reach, combo counter, day counter, memory and server address. Drag them anywhere in “Edit HUD layout”.
New in the Right Shift menu: toggle sneak, no hurt camera shake, no view bobbing and max brightness — turning one off gives you your own setting back.
Pick the accent and HUD text colour, turn the text shadow on or off, and copy your coordinates in one click.
The menu is now split into HUD, Features and Style, and fits smaller windows.
Your Discord status follows what you do: the page you’re on in Solaris, the main menu, your singleplayer world, the server you joined, or hosting a world for friends.
Hosting a server shows it on Discord with the player count (like “2 of 10”) and the address to join.
Privacy settings and streamer mode apply instantly, and Solaris never sends Discord more updates than it allows.
You can now wear Minecraft’s default skins (Steve, Alex and the others) — the Wear button used to stay greyed out.
A skin Mojang accepted no longer shows an error when Mojang is slow to update your profile.
The Skins page follows you when you switch accounts, and says when you’re already wearing the selected skin.
A server left running after Solaris closed or updated no longer blocks the next start with “Address already in use” — Solaris closes the old copy first, or tells you what is using the port.
New servers add you to the whitelist and as an operator, so you can’t be locked out of your own server.
When someone is turned away by the whitelist, Solaris tells you and offers “Add to whitelist”.
The Players tab updates when someone joins or leaves, renamed servers update right away, and crash messages say which server stopped.

title: Solaris on Linux, faster and steadier

entries.text: Solaris now runs on Linux (64-bit): download the AppImage (any distro) or the .deb (Ubuntu, Debian, Mint, Pop!_OS). Both update themselves like on Windows.
Games, Java, mods, modpacks, skins, server hosting (including playit.gg and live CPU/RAM stats) all work on Linux.
Finds the Java installed by your distro, and on laptops with two graphics cards can run Minecraft on the fast one.
Starts normally on Ubuntu 24.04 and newer, where many Electron apps fail to open.
Game and server consoles no longer slow the launcher down while big modpacks start: log lines are drawn in batches.
Mod lists open faster: mod names and icons are remembered between sessions instead of re-reading every jar.
Solaris opens a little faster, and Java detection checks all Javas at once.
“Clean up storage” no longer deletes the OptiFine versions you imported or the running playit.gg agent.
A stuck internet connection can no longer freeze “Downloading game files” forever — Solaris retries instead.
Stopping a server while it was still preparing Java now really stops it.
Sending a command to a server at the moment it closed could crash Solaris in the background.
Server backups on Paper and Purpur no longer store the Nether and End twice.
Closing the window while hosting and playing no longer shuts your server down when the game closes.
Moving the data folder is blocked while games or servers run, and into a folder inside itself.
The right native libraries are picked for your computer’s processor.
The Solaris Client now has its own mod, made by Solaris: press Right Shift in game for the Solaris menu.
Movable HUD: FPS, CPS, keystrokes, coordinates with direction, ping and a clock. Drag them anywhere in “Edit HUD layout”.
Hold C to zoom, and turn on toggle sprint from the Solaris menu. Your settings are saved.
OneConfig, EvergreenHUD, PolySprint and Zoomify are now optional extras (off by default) — the Solaris mod does those jobs.

title: Hosting: every server type, playit.gg, backups and more

entries.text: Create Vanilla, Paper, Purpur, Fabric, Forge and NeoForge servers — pick the version, memory, max players, port and folder. Solaris downloads everything.
Public address with playit.gg for any server type (free account, connected once), or e4mc for Fabric/Forge/NeoForge (no account). Tunnel status and automatic reconnects.
Dashboard with status, players, CPU, RAM, uptime and address. Start, stop, restart, open folder, settings and delete.
Server page: live console (clear, auto-scroll, errors only), players, whitelist and operators, worlds, backups and restore, log files, and a full server.properties editor.
Install mods and plugins from Modrinth, checked against your server’s version and software — or start a server from a modpack.
Skins now really change: each wardrobe skin has a Wear button, and the skin you wear is marked. Clicking a skin only previews it.
Your current skin is read live from your Microsoft account, so a new skin shows right away instead of a minute later.
Deleting an instance removes it for good instead of moving it to the Recycle Bin.

title: Host servers, in-game client menu and skins that show up

entries.text: New Host page: create a Minecraft server on your PC in a few clicks, start it, and share a public address — no port forwarding, no account. Live console, players, kick, settings, whitelist.
Solaris stops your servers properly when you quit, so worlds are saved.
In-game client menu like Lunar: press Right Shift for one menu with your mods, a HUD editor and settings (OneConfig by Polyfrost).
New modules: PolySprint (toggle sprint/sneak) and Chatting (chat tabs and search).
“Wear this skin” now checks with Mojang that your skin really changed, and tells you clearly if it didn’t.
Offline accounts can wear skins too — Solaris adds CustomSkinLoader to modded instances so your skin shows in game.
Installing a mod, pack or shader now turns the button green with “Installed” and a check, so you know it worked.
New icons from Lucide.
Player look-ups fall back to minetools when Mojang is busy.
World hosting picks up the e4mc address even when it is hidden in chat.

title: New look, OptiFine, hosting for friends and cosmetics

entries.text: New Solaris logo and new fonts (Plus Jakarta Sans and Outfit) — including a cleaner Play button.
Faster start: Home shows modpacks, news and player counts from last time instantly, and the 3D skin viewer only loads when you need it.
Optional cosmetics: Capes (see OptiFine, LabyMod and MinecraftCapes capes), 3D Skin Layers, Wavey Capes, Emotecraft and Ears.
Host for friends: with e4mc, Open to LAN puts your world online without port forwarding. Solaris shows the address and an invite link.
New modules like Feather and OneClient: EvergreenHUD (FPS, CPS, keystrokes), Controlling, FastQuit, Chat Heads, World Host, More Culling and more.
AppleSkin’s settings page works again (Cloth Config is added automatically).
Play together: host your world, join a friend by address or invite link, and see when you are hosting.
OptiFine for vanilla instances: download OptiFine from optifine.net, import it, and Solaris installs it. Pick OptiFine when creating an instance or in Change version.
See the release notes of a new version while it downloads, before you restart.

title: Minecraft news, solaris:// links and snowfall

entries.text: Minecraft news: the latest Java Edition news from Mojang right on Home. Click a card to read the full article.
New animated splash screen while Solaris starts.
solaris:// links open Solaris straight to a Modrinth modpack (solaris://modrinth/<name>) or offer to join a server (solaris://server/<address>). Links never install or launch anything without you.
Snowfall: gentle falling snow, on by itself in December. Switch it in Settings → Appearance.
Update files are now named Solaris-Setup-x.y.z.exe, so releases upload to GitHub without renaming.

title: Sign-in screen, self-updates and Discord buttons

entries.text: New sign-in screen: sign in with Microsoft or pick an offline name before you start, with a live 3D preview of your player.
Solaris now updates itself: new versions download in the background with a progress animation, then install with one click.
“What’s new” pops up once after each update.
No more “Update failed” message when there simply isn’t a new version yet.
Rich Presence works out of the box — no application ID to paste. It now uses Silent Client’s discord-rpc, shows a “Get Solaris” button and reconnects by itself when you open Discord later.
Animated capes in the 3D viewer, and a button to preview your own cape file (idea from Silent Client’s skinview3d).

title: CurseForge, friends and a lot more

entries.text: CurseForge: browse and install mods, modpacks, shaders and resource packs (add your free API key in Settings → Integrations).
Modpack updates: update a Modrinth or CurseForge modpack, or switch to any version. Your worlds, settings and own mods are kept.
Source badges show where every mod came from: Modrinth, CurseForge, a modpack, or added by you.
Import CurseForge modpack .zip files and CurseForge app instances.
New Files, Screenshots and Logs tabs: a built-in file explorer and config editor, per-instance screenshots, and crash logs you can upload to mclo.gs.
Reorder or hide instance tabs in Settings → Appearance.
Damaged game files are detected automatically and repaired on the next launch.
Friends: follow players, see their real skins, and see when Solaris spots them on a server.
New mods are scanned for malware automatically, plus Scan now in Settings → Privacy & safety.
Discord shows your player head for Microsoft accounts, with privacy switches for what is shared.
Refresh skin button, streamer mode, and warnings for unusual offline usernames.
Light, dark or match-system mode, a Classic layout, and custom gradients for buttons and the background.
Low-end PC mode and a GPU acceleration switch in Settings → Performance.
Smarter Java: per-version Java choices, a Test button, and Java that is too old is skipped automatically.
If your moved data folder is missing (e.g. an unplugged drive), Solaris asks what to do instead of starting empty.
Launch every Minecraft: Java Edition release, snapshot and old version from one launcher.
Multi-instancing: run several instances at the same time, each with its own live console.
Automatic Java: the right official Java runtime is downloaded for every version.
Quick Play: join a server or open a world straight from the launcher.
Auto memory sizing based on your system RAM, with per-instance overrides.
Performance mode and dedicated-GPU preference for laptops.
Fabric, Quilt, Forge, NeoForge and Legacy Fabric — loaders only show up on compatible versions.
Duplicate instances with selective copying of mods, packs, worlds and config.
Share instances as .solpack files and import .mrpack modpacks by drag & drop.
Custom icons, pinned favourites, readable folder names and play-time tracking.
Import from the official launcher, MultiMC and Prism Launcher.
Built-in Modrinth browser for mods, modpacks, resource packs, shaders and datapacks.
Version picker, automatic required dependencies and multi-category filters.
Bulk select, enable, disable and delete with Ctrl/Shift+Click.
Update manager that checks every mod against Modrinth by file hash.
Duplicate-mod detection and a heuristic malware scan.
One-click all-in-one modpack: Sodium, Lithium, FerriteCore, Zoomify and more, kept up to date on every launch.
Toggle modules per instance from the Solaris Client page.
Server browser with live player counts, ping, MOTD, region & tag filters and favourites.
Server statistics: player count history for every server you check.
Skin wardrobe with a 3D preview, staged Apply, and cape switching for Microsoft accounts.
Discord Rich Presence.
Crash assistant explains crashes in plain language with suggested fixes and hex exit codes.
Live console with filtering and one-click log sharing to mclo.gs.
Hosts-file check for blocked Mojang/Microsoft domains.
Themes with live preview, custom accent colours and a custom theme editor.
Editable keybinds, mouse back/forward navigation and instant language switching.
Gallery of screenshots across all instances.
Storage manager: see what uses space, clean up unused files and move the data folder.
